uncited: **Identify Ambiguity:** Determine if the current cube case involves an ambiguous face.
*   Let the vertices of the ambiguous face be $v_a, v_b, v_c, v_d$.
If $\bar{v} > I$, the surface is closer to the "inside" vertices; if $\bar{v} < I$, it is closer to the "outside" vertices.
*   Select the topology based on this estimated sign.
*   **Multiple Ambiguous Faces:** A cube can have more than one ambiguous face.
*   **When to Use:** Use Facial Average for simple, smooth data.
Use Gradient methods for higher accuracy requirements.
